companions.name: NGC 6362 V41 B
companions.description: The secondary star of the eclipsing binary NGC 6362 V41, 0.728 solar masses and 0.7307 solar radii; the two stars eclipse each other every 17.889 days.

radius.source: Secondary radius (solar radii) 0.7307 +/- 0.0046, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Kaluzny et al. (2015AJ....150..155K)

mass.source: Secondary mass (solar masses) 0.728 +/- 0.0047, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Kaluzny et al. (2015AJ....150..155K)

temperature.source: Secondary log Teff 3.759 +/- 0.009, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Kaluzny et al. (2015AJ....150..155K): 5741 K

orbit.source: NGC 6362 V41: P 17.8888441 d and primary-eclipse time HJD 2454263.65242 (Section II.1, before Equation (2)); i 89.547 degrees (Table 4, column V41); e 0.3125, omega 321.23 degrees (Table 4, column V41); used as published: fitting the paper's Table 3 radial velocities with it leaves 0.59 km/s rms against 29 km/s for omega + 180 (V40 needs + 180 only because the paper counts V40's phase from its secondary minimum). HJD is taken as BJD_TDB (under a minute apart); at the primary eclipse the secondary is in front, the component these papers call primary being the one eclipsed at phase 0. Separation from Kepler's third law with DEBCat's masses

text.card: The secondary star of NGC 6362 V41, a pair that eclipse each other every 17.889 days.
text.introduction: It has 0.728 solar masses and 0.7307 solar radii; its partner has 0.8215 and 1.0739, measured from the eclipses and the stars' motions.
text.locator: DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164), NGC 6362 V41: Mass, Radius and Period, from Kaluzny et al. (2015AJ....150..155K)
